open_points.subject: effects deciding approvals/resolutions against run end state
open_points.text: "Whether an approval or an attempt can be decided now — `requested`, `unknown`, its run not ended — is checked by `effects` (A10 rule 3, A11 rule 3)."
open_points.question: How does `effects` obtain the authoritative "run not ended" fact when run lifecycle/state ownership is in `runs`, which is on a later dependency line?
options: `runs` must perform the run-ended gate before calling `effects` decision capabilities
`effects` may read run status directly from `store` and treat it as authoritative for this check
`store` must expose a dedicated run-ended predicate owned below `effects`
open_points.default_guess: `effects` reads run status directly from `store` and checks final/non-final itself.

open_points.subject: instance validity checks during operation send
open_points.text: "`bindings.check_binding_current`, which returns the current ManifestOperation M10 — method, path, key fields, effect class, and the `api_base_url`, `required_headers` and class of the instance whose name `installation.selected_instance_name` gives (A08 rule 2) — or `binding_stale`; then `service_invoker.prepare_request` with that operation, which checks the instance..."
open_points.question: At send time, which module owns failure outcomes for missing/invalid selected instance data: `bindings` (while producing ManifestOperation) or `service_invoker` (during prepare)?
options: `bindings.check_binding_current` fails before `prepare_request` when instance data is absent/invalid
`service_invoker.prepare_request` is the sole owner of instance/address/class checks
checks are split (e.g., missing instance in `bindings`, URL/TLS policy in `service_invoker`)
open_points.default_guess: `service_invoker.prepare_request` owns all instance/address/class send-time checks; `bindings` only checks staleness/invocability of the pinned operation entry.

open_points.subject: startup removal of ended-run spools
open_points.text: State 2 A18 rule 4: "On start, temporary files and the spool directories of runs that ended and do not keep their spool (A14) are removed; nothing else is." State 3 start order: "`runs.recover_running_runs`, which first names to `store.remove_run_spool` every ended run that no longer keeps its spool..."
open_points.question: Which module is responsible for deciding and executing ended-run spool cleanup at startup: `store.open_store` directly, or `runs.recover_running_runs` via `store.remove_run_spool`?
options: `store.open_store` removes ended-run spools autonomously during store startup
`runs.recover_running_runs` decides targets and instructs `store` to remove them
both perform cleanup with different scopes
open_points.default_guess: `runs.recover_running_runs` decides eligible runs from run records and calls `store.remove_run_spool`; `store.open_store` removes only temporary/unlinked leftovers.
